liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Iko Iko** (2 reviews): The set opens with this song, a unique choice for the date; Jerry sings a half-step behind, making the version sound stuck in muck [5][6]
- **Row Jimmy** (1 review): The performance is compared to wading in a senior's wading pool [6]
- **Bird Song** (1 review): This performance is described as a serious beast with excellent energy [15]
- **Hell In A Bucket** (1 review): The crowd joined Bobby on lyrics, marking an excellent close to set one [15]
- **Foolish Heart** (1 review): The source singles out this performance as being very good [5]

## The recordings

- **gd88-12-11.aud.willy.16095.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 19 songs; 127 min; rated 3.31/5 by 13 [1]. Said about its sound: The recording is described as a high-quality audience tape; The audio is filtered, limiting the clarity of the performance; The audience recording is listenable and captures crowd reactions clearly [5][6][9]
- **gd1988-12-11.152147.ultramatrix.miller.flc1644**: soundboard; 18 songs; 127 min [2]
- **gd1988-12-11.151093.aud.lohr.vernon.flac2496**: audience recording; 18 songs; 121 min [3]
- **gd1988-12-11.151092.aud.lohr.vernon.flac1648**: audience recording; 18 songs; 121 min [4]

## Around the show

- LAPD officers screamed through the parking lot, busting heads during the event [8]
- The band was kicked out of most major Southern California venues at the time [8]
- The crowd claps along, which is essential for enjoying the Iko performance [9]
- The camping area's shakedown street provided a really fun experience for attendees [11]
- The audience displayed high energy and brotherly love, contributing to the night's success [12]
- Brent took over the stage space while Jerry appeared lazy and uninspired [13]
- Local DJ Michael Slavko, known as M. Dung, was present at the venue [13]
- While not transcendent, most attendees left the arena happy with the show [10]
- The Long Beach show was comparable to the earlier Laguna Seca performances [11]
- The entire run is characterized as phoning it in with low energy [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd88-12-11.aud.willy.16095.sbeok.shnf**: source: AUD>DAT>CD [1]. Also: The tape was transferred from AUD to DAT to CD via Paul B; Willy seeded the recording to etree [1]
- **gd1988-12-11.152147.ultramatrix.miller.flc1644**: taped by Steve Marcus; transferred by Mastered by Charlie Miller  March 27, 2021; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (Don Pearson) > Cassette (Dolby C) > WAV (16-bit/44.1k) [2]. Also: Steve Marcus provided the recording, with Willy supplying the patch source [2]
- **gd1988-12-11.151093.aud.lohr.vernon.flac2496**: taped by Gesine Lohr; transferred by Matt Vernon; source: Unknown mics > DAT > MAC [3]
- **gd1988-12-11.151092.aud.lohr.vernon.flac1648**: taped by Gesine Lohr; transferred by Matt Vernon; source: Unknown mics > DAT > MAC [4]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1988-12-11 Grateful Dead Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1988-12-11-grateful-dead-backstage-pass/) [18]
- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1988-12-11 Grateful Dead Ticket - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1988-12-11-grateful-dead-ticket/) [19]
